title: Examples
text: event time follows Weibull distribution shape parameter \(\alpha = 2\) scale parameter \(\lambda_{T^*} = 10\), \[ T^*\sim \text{Weibull}(\alpha, \lambda_{T^*}). \] random censoring time follows exponential distribution rate parameter \(\lambda_{C_{rnd}}\), \[ C_{\text{rnd}}\sim \text{Exp}(\lambda_{C_{rnd}}) \] leading \(S_{C_{\text{rnd}}}(t) = \exp(-\lambda_{C_{rnd}} t)\) \(f_{C_{\text{rnd}}}(t) = \lambda_{C_{rnd}} \exp(-\lambda_{C_{rnd}} t)\). default package use exponential censoring, need specify survival function event time. default bounds \(\lambda_{C_{rnd}}\) parameter c 10^{-5}. can now simulate data.
code: lambda_evt <- 0.1 shape <- 2  event_surv <- \(t) 1 - pweibull(t, shape = shape, scale = 1 / lambda_evt)  lambda_c_50 <- find_cens_param(pc_target, event_surv) lambda_c_50 #> $parameter #> [1] 0.0338 #>  #> $cens_prop #> [1] 0.2500012 n <- 10**6  event_times <- rweibull(n, shape = shape, scale = 1 / lambda_evt) censoring_times <- rexp(n, rate = lambda_c_50$parameter)  observed_times <- pmin(event_times, censoring_times) censoring_indicators <- as.integer(event_times <= censoring_times) mean(censoring_indicators == 0) #> [1] 0.249808

what: Weibull with Exponential Censoring and Covariates
title: Examples
text: event time follows Weibull distribution shape parameter \(\alpha = 2\) scale parameter \(\lambda_{T^*} = 10*\exp(-0.5 * x1 + 0.3 * x2 * \text{trt} - 0.2 * \text{trt})\), \[ T^*\mid\mathbf{X}\sim \text{Weibull}(\alpha, \lambda_{T^*}). \] random censoring time follows exponential distribution rate parameter \(\lambda_{C_{rnd}}\), \[ C_{\text{rnd}}\sim\text{Exp}(\lambda_{C_{rnd}}). \] three covariates: standard normal covariate \(X_1\sim\text{N}(0,1)\), uniform covariate \(X_2 \sim \text{U}(0,1)\) binary treatment indicator \(\text{trt}\sim\text{B}(0.5)\). warnings caused numerical integration bounds \((-\infty, \infty)\) covariate \(X_1\) inserted. affect result. can now simulate data.
code: lambda_evt <- \(x1, x2, trt) 0.1 * exp((-0.5 * x1 + 0.3 * x2 * trt - 0.2 * trt)) cov_dens <- \(x1, x2, trt) dnorm(x1) * dunif(x2, 0, 1) * dbinom(trt, 1, 0.5)  # Note that we give the bounds for trt as a list, # because it is a discrete variable.  cov_bounds <- list(   x1 = c(-Inf, Inf),   x2 = c(0, 1),   trt = list(0, 1) ) shape <- 2  event_surv <- function(t, x1, x2, trt) {   1 - pweibull(t, shape = shape, scale = 1 / lambda_evt(x1, x2, trt)) }  # This will take a bit longer to compute lambda_c_50 <- find_cens_param(pc_target, event_surv,   covariate_density = cov_dens,   covariate_bounds = cov_bounds ) lambda_c_50 #> $parameter #> [1] 0.03049219 #>  #> $cens_prop #> [1] 0.25 n <- 10**6  cov_data <- data.frame(   x1 = rnorm(n),   x2 = runif(n, 0, 1),   trt = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5) ) event_times <- rweibull(   n,   shape = shape,   scale = 1 / lambda_evt(     cov_data$x1,     cov_data$x2,     cov_data$trt   ) ) censoring_times <- rexp(n, rate = lambda_c_50$parameter)  observed_times <- pmin(event_times, censoring_times) censoring_indicators <- as.integer(event_times <= censoring_times) mean(censoring_indicators == 0) #> [1] 0.250179

title: Examples
text: first use CensRCalc::estimate_cens_prop() see effect different censoring parameters proportion censoring. lognormal distributed event time parameters \(\mu_{T^*} = 6\) \(\sigma_{T^*} = 1.1\), \[ T^* \sim \text{LN}(\mu_{T^*}, \sigma_{T^*}) \leftrightarrow \ln(T^*) \sim \text{N}(\mu_{T^*}, \sigma_{T^*}). \] Also random censoring lognormal distributed fixed \(\sigma_C = 1.2\) \(\mu_C = \lambda_C\) parameter interest, \[ C \sim \text{LN}(\lambda_C, \sigma_C). \]  can now simulate data.
code: event_surv <- \(t) 1 - plnorm(t, meanlog = 6, sdlog = 1.1) cens_sdlog <- 1.2 cens_surv <- \(t, mean) 1 - plnorm(t, meanlog = mean, sdlog = cens_sdlog) cens_dens <- \(t, mean) dlnorm(t, meanlog = mean, sdlog = cens_sdlog)  bounds <- c(0.1, 10)  est_fun <- estimate_cens_prop(event_surv,   cens_survival = cens_surv,   cens_density = cens_dens,   target_bounds = bounds,   target = "mean" )  x <- seq(bounds[1], bounds[2], length.out = 50) y <- sapply(x, est_fun) mean_c_50 <- find_cens_param(pc_target, event_surv,   cens_survival = cens_surv,   cens_density = cens_dens,   target = "mean",   target_bounds = bounds )  plot(   x,   y,   type = "l",   xlab = "Mean of log(Censoring Time)",   ylab = "Proportion Censored" ) points(mean_c_50$parameter, pc_target, col = "red", pch = 19) n <- 10**6  event_times <- rlnorm(n, meanlog = 6, sdlog = 1.1) censoring_times <- rlnorm(n, meanlog = mean_c_50$parameter, sdlog = cens_sdlog)  observed_times <- pmin(event_times, censoring_times) censoring_indicators <- as.integer(event_times <= censoring_times) mean(censoring_indicators == 0) #> [1] 0.250447

what: Weibull with Exponential Censoring, Covariates, Administrative Censoring and Accrual
title: Examples
text: previous example, event time follows Weibull distribution shape parameter \(\alpha = 2\) scale parameter \(\lambda_{T^*} = 10*\exp(-0.5 * x1 + 0.3 * x2 * \text{trt} - 0.2 * \text{trt})\), \[ T^*\mid\mathbf{X}\sim \text{Weibull}(\alpha, \lambda_{T^*}). \] random censoring time follows exponential distribution rate parameter \(\lambda_{C_{rnd}}\), \[ C_{\text{rnd}}\sim \text{Exp}(\lambda_{C_{rnd}}) \] leading \(S_{C_{\text{rnd}}}(t) = \exp(-\lambda_{C_{rnd}} t)\) \(f_{C_{\text{rnd}}}(t) = \lambda_{C_{rnd}} \exp(-\lambda_{C_{rnd}} t)\). three covariates: standard normal covariate \(X_1\sim\text {N}(0,1)\), uniform covariate \(X_2 \sim \text{U}(0,1)\) binary treatment indicator \(\text{trt}\sim\text{B}(0.5)\). addition, accrual time \(\tau_{\text{acc}} = 1\) administrative censoring time \(\tau_{\text{adm}} = 3\), inducing random administrative censoring variable \[ C_{\text{adm}}\sim \text{U}(2,3) \] \(S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(t) = 3-t\) \(f_{C_{\text{adm}}}(t) = 1\). warnings caused numerical integration bounds \((-\infty, \infty)\) covariate \(X_1\) inserted. affect result. can now simulate data. Instead overall censoring proportion \(P(C < T^*)\), can also evaluate censoring proportion specific time point \(\tau\) \(P(C < \tau \mid T^* > \tau)=1-S_{C_{\text{obs}}}(t)\).
code: lambda_evt <- \(x1, x2, trt) 0.1 * exp((-0.5 * x1 + 0.3 * x2 * trt - 0.2 * trt)) cov_dens <- \(x1, x2, trt) dnorm(x1) * dunif(x2, 0, 1) * dbinom(trt, 1, 0.5)  # Note that we give the bounds for trt as a list, # because it is a discrete variable.  cov_bounds <- list(   x1 = c(-Inf, Inf),   x2 = c(0, 1),   trt = list(0, 1) ) shape <- 2  event_surv <- function(t, x1, x2, trt) {   1 - pweibull(t, shape = shape, scale = 1 / lambda_evt(x1, x2, trt)) }  time_acc <- 10 time_adm <- 20  lambda_c_50 <- find_cens_param(pc_target, event_surv,   covariate_density = cov_dens,   covariate_bounds = cov_bounds,   time_admin_cens = time_adm,   time_accrual = time_acc ) lambda_c_50 #> $parameter #> [1] 0.005809193 #>  #> $cens_prop #> [1] 0.2499994 n <- 10**6  cov_data <- data.frame(   x1 = rnorm(n),   x2 = runif(n, 0, 1),   trt = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5) ) event_times <- rweibull(   n,   shape = shape,   scale = 1 / lambda_evt(     cov_data$x1,     cov_data$x2,     cov_data$trt   ) ) rnd_censoring_times <- rexp(n, rate = lambda_c_50$parameter) adm_censoring_times <- runif(n, time_adm - time_acc, time_adm)  censoring_times <- pmin(rnd_censoring_times, adm_censoring_times) observed_times <- pmin(event_times, censoring_times) censoring_indicators <- as.integer(event_times <= censoring_times) mean(censoring_indicators == 0) #> [1] 0.249912 taus <- seq(0, 30, length.out = 50)  estimator <- estimate_cens_prop(event_surv,   covariate_density = cov_dens,   covariate_bounds = cov_bounds,   time_admin_cens = time_adm,   time_accrual = time_acc )  cens_p_num <- sapply(taus, \(tau) estimator(lambda_c_50$parameter, tau = tau))  # Based on the simulated data: cens_p_sim <- sapply(taus, \(tau) {   mean(censoring_indicators == 0 & observed_times <= tau) })  plot(taus, cens_p_num,   type = "l", col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.5), lwd = 2,   xlab = "Time", ylab = "Censoring Proportion" ) lines(taus, cens_p_sim, col = rgb(1, 0, 0, 0.5), lwd = 2) legend("bottomright",   legend = c("Numerical Integration", "Simulation"),   col = c(rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.5), rgb(1, 0, 0, 0.5)), lwd = 2 )

title: Full Details and Usage
text: First, consider special case patients accrued time, .e. start clinical trial. assume independent censoring, .e. event time conditional \(d\)-dimensional covariate vector \(\mathbf{X}\), \(T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}\sim F_{T^*\mid\mathbf{X}}\), independent random censoring time \(C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\sim F_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}\) \(\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) parameter random censoring distribution: \[\begin{equation*}     T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X} \perp\!\!\!\perp C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}} \end{equation*}\] administrative censoring time \(\tau_{\text{adm}}\) fixed. Thus, actual censoring time \(C\) minimum random censoring time \(C_{\text{rnd}}\) administrative censoring time \(\tau_{\text{adm}}\): \[\begin{equation*}     C := \min(C_{\text{rnd}}, \tau_{\text{adm}}) \end{equation*}\] observed time \(T\) minimum event time \(T^{*}\) censoring time \(C\): \[\begin{equation*}     T := \min(T^{*}, C) \end{equation*}\] event indicator given : \[\begin{equation*}     \delta := (T^{*} \leq C) = \begin{cases}         1 & \text{, } T^{*} \leq C \\         0 & \text{, otherwise}     \end{cases} \end{equation*}\] Let \(p_{C}\) target value expected censoring proportion. goal calculate parameter \(\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) random censoring distribution \(F_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) expected censoring proportion simulated dataset \(p_{C}\). , derive formula \(\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) depending expected censoring proportion \(p_{C}\) parameters event time distribution \(F_{T^{*}}\) well administrative censoring time \(\tau_{\text{adm}}\). leads equation can solved \(\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) root finding problem. start probability censoring given subject, \(P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X})\). Using assumption independent censoring know \[\begin{align*}     P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) &= P(\{C_{\text{rnd}} \leq T^{*}, C_{\text{rnd}} \leq \tau_{\text{adm}}\} \vee \{\tau_{\text{adm}} < T^{*}, \tau_{\text{adm}} < C_{\text{rnd}}\}\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) \\                       &= P(C_{\text{rnd}} \leq T^{*}, C_{\text{rnd}} \leq \tau_{\text{adm}}\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) + P(\tau_{\text{adm}} < T^{*}, \tau_{\text{adm}} < C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) \\                       &= P(C_{\text{rnd}} \leq \min(T^{*}, \tau_{\text{adm}})\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) + P(\tau_{\text{adm}} < T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X})P(\tau_{\text{adm}} < C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) \\                       &= \!\begin{aligned}[t]                             &\int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} P(c \leq T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X})dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c) + \\                             &P(\tau_{\text{adm}} < T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X})P(\tau_{\text{adm}} < C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}})                          \end{aligned} \\                       &= \int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c)dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c) + S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(\tau_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(\tau_{\text{adm}}) \\                       &= \int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c)f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c)dc + S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(\tau_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(\tau_{\text{adm}}) \end{align*}\] \(S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}\) \(S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}\) survival functions event time random censoring time conditional covariate vector \(\mathbf{X}\) random censoring parameter \(\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\), respectively. first term (integral) describes probability random censoring administrative censoring. second term describes probability administrative censoring happens event random censoring. Note \(P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}})\) random variable takes values depending covariates \(\mathbf{X}\) specific subject. Now integrate \(P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}})\) covariate distribution \(F_{X}\) get probability censoring simulated dataset, independent covariates specific subject: \[\begin{equation*}     P(\delta = 0\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) = E_{X}(P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}})) = \int_{D_{X}} P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}=x, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) dF_{X} = \int_{D_{X}} P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}=x, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}})f_{X}(x) dx, \end{equation*}\] \(D_{X}\) domain covariate vector \(X\). d-dimensional integral must usually computed numerically. packages help(calculus) help(cubature) used purpose. Now can solve \(\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) using root finding algorithm. function solved given : \[\begin{equation*}     P(\delta = 0\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) = p_{C} \Longleftrightarrow P(\delta = 0\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) - p_{C} = 0. \end{equation*}\] solve root finding problem use stats::uniroot function implements bracketing root finding algorithm.

text: general case, patients accrued within time span \([0, \tau_{\text{acc}}]\). consider uniform distributed accrual times thus, random accrual time \(R \sim U([0, \tau_{\text{acc}}])\). parameters variables identical special case. Stochastically, random process accrual can equivalently modelled making administrative censoring time random variable, \(C_{\text{adm}}\), given following definition: \[\begin{equation*}     C_{\text{adm}} := \tau_{\text{adm}} - R. \end{equation*}\] words, accrual patient can observed administrative censoring time reached. Consequently, time patient can observed accrual, follow-time, given difference administrative censoring time actual accrual time patient. follows \(C_{\text{adm}} \sim U([\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}, \tau_{\text{adm}}])\). Furthermore, assume independence \(T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}\) \(C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) well \(C_{\text{adm}}\): \[\begin{equation*}     T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X} \perp\!\!\!\perp C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}} \quad \wedge \quad T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X} \perp\!\!\!\perp C_{\text{adm}} \end{equation*}\] , start probability censoring given subject: \[\begin{align*}     P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) &= P(\{C_{\text{rnd}} < T^{*}, C_{\text{rnd}} < C_{\text{adm}}\} \vee \{C_{\text{adm}} < T^{*}, C_{\text{adm}} < C_{\text{rnd}}\}\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) \\                                         &= P(C_{\text{rnd}} < T^{*}, C_{\text{rnd}} < C_{\text{adm}}\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) + P(C_{\text{adm}} < T^{*}, C_{\text{adm}} < C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) \\                                         &= \!\begin{aligned}[t]                                                 &\int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} P(c_{\text{rnd}} < T^{*}, c_{\text{rnd}} < C_{\text{adm}}\mid\mathbf{X})dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) + \\                                                 &\int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} P(c_{\text{adm}} < T^{*}, c_{\text{adm}} < C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}})dF_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{adm}})                                             \end{aligned} \\                                         &= \!\begin{aligned}[t]                                                 &\int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} P(c_{\text{rnd}} < T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X})P(c_{\text{rnd}} < c_{\text{adm}}) dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) + \\                                                 &\int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} P(c_{\text{adm}} < T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X})P(c_{\text{adm}} < C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) dF_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{adm}})                                             \end{aligned} \\                                         &= \!\begin{aligned}[t]                                                 &\int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} P(c_{\text{rnd}} < T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X})P(c_{\text{rnd}} < c_{\text{adm}}) dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) + \\                                                 &\int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} P(C_{\text{adm}} < T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X})P(C_{\text{adm}} < C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) dF_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{adm}})                                             \end{aligned} \\                                         &= \!\begin{aligned}[t]                                                 &\int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) + \\                                                 &\int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) dF_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{adm}})                                             \end{aligned} \\                                         &=: I_{\text{rnd}} + I_{\text{adm}}                                                  \end{align*}\] \(I_{\text{rnd}}\) describes random censoring \(I_{\text{adm}}\) administrative censoring. Since \(C_{\text{adm}} \[\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}, \tau_{\text{adm}}]\) \(P(c_{\text{rnd}} < C_{\text{adm}}) = S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) = 1\) \(c_{\text{rnd}} \(0, \tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}})\). can rewrite \(I_{\text{rnd}}\): \[\begin{equation*}     I_{\text{rnd}} = \int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) +               \int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) \end{equation*}\] gives us: \[\begin{align*}     P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) &= \!\begin{aligned}[t]                                                 &\int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) + \\                                                 &\int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) + \\                                                 &\int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) dF_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{adm}})                                             \end{aligned} \\                                         &= \!\begin{aligned}[t]                                                 &\int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} + \\                                                 &\int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} + \\                                                 &\int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - title: Full Details and Usage
text: Lastly, consider two edge cases, \(\tau_{\text{acc}} = 0\) \(\tau_{\text{adm}} = \infty\). first case, accrual time span zero, .e. patients accrued beginning study. general formula collapse special formula showed . \(\tau_{\text{acc}} = 0\) follows \(C_{\text{adm}} \sim U([\tau_{\text{adm}}, \tau_{\text{adm}}]) = \delta_{\tau_{\text{adm}}}\), \(\delta_{\tau_{\text{adm}}}\) Dirac distribution \(\tau_{\text{adm}}\). follows: \[\begin{align*}     I_{\text{adm}} &= \int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) dF_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) \\     &= \int_{\tau_{\text{adm}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) d\delta_{\tau_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) \\     &= \int_{\{\tau_{\text{adm}}\}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) d\delta_{\tau_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) \\     &= S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(\tau_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(\tau_{\text{adm}}) \end{align*}\] \(I_{\text{rnd,adm}}\) : \[\begin{align*}     I_{\text{rnd,adm}} = \int_{\tau_{\text{adm}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c)S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c) dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c) = \int_{\{\tau_{\text{adm}}\}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c)S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c) dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c) = 0 \end{align*}\] \(F_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}\) continuous distribution function (hence, continuous measure), integral one point zero. \(\tau_{\text{acc}} = 0\) get: \[\begin{equation*}     P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) = \int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c)f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c)dc + S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(\tau_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(\tau_{\text{adm}}) \end{equation*}\] special case saw Censoring without accrual. second case, administrative censoring time infinite, .e. patients observed event random censoring occurs. results three improper integrals general formula. can solve considering limit integrals \(\tau_{\text{adm}} \\infty\). First take look \(I_{\text{rnd}}\). \(\tau_{\text{adm}} \\infty\), \(\tau_{\text{adm}}-\tau_{\text{acc}} \\infty\). : \[\begin{align*}     I_{\text{rnd,adm}} &= \int_{\infty}^{\infty} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) \\     &= \lim_{\\infty} \int_{}^{} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dF_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) \\     &= \lim_{\\infty} 0 = 0. \end{align*}\] Next, consider \(I_{\text{adm}}\). \(\tau_{\text{adm}} \\infty\), \(C_{\text{adm}} \sim U([\infty, \infty]) = \delta_{\infty} = \lim_{\\infty} \delta_{}\). follows: \[\begin{align*}     I_{\text{adm}} &= \int_{\infty}^{\infty} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) dF_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) \\     &= \lim_{\\infty} \int_{}^{} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) d\delta_{}(c_{\text{adm}}) \\     &= \lim_{\\infty} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}()S_{    C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}() = 0. \end{align*}\] Note \(\lim_{\\infty} S_{X}() = 0\) every continuous survival function \(S_{X}\). , \(\tau_{\text{adm}} \\infty\) general formula collapses : \[\begin{equation*}     P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) = \int_{0}^{\infty} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} \end{equation*}\] see \(\tau_{\text{adm}} \\infty\), accrual time affect calculation censoring parameter. words, accrual time becomes irrelevant patient observed event random censoring.

Set logger to DEBUG level estimator <- estimate_cens_prop(event_surv, cov_dens, cov_bounds,   time_accrual = tau_acc,   time_admin_cens = tau_adm,   cens_surv = cens_surv,   cens_dens = cens_dens,   target_bounds = bounds ) #> DEBUG [2026-07-24 07:32:01] Density total integral calculated as: 0.999559635073658 #> DEBUG [2026-07-24 07:32:01] Density total integral calculated as: 0.999559635073658 #> DEBUG [2026-07-24 07:32:01] Density total integral calculated as: 0.999999903558124 #> DEBUG [2026-07-24 07:32:01] Density total integral calculated as: 0.999999903558124 #> DEBUG [2026-07-24 07:32:01] Density total integral calculated as: 0.999999998533039 #> DEBUG [2026-07-24 07:32:01] Density total integral calculated as: 0.999999998533039 #> DEBUG [2026-07-24 07:32:01] Density total integral calculated as: 0.999999977140023 #> DEBUG [2026-07-24 07:32:01] Density total integral calculated as: 0.999999977140023 #> DEBUG [2026-07-24 07:32:01] Density total integral calculated as: 1.00000017787208 #> DEBUG [2026-07-24 07:32:01] Density total integral calculated as: 1.00000017787208 log_threshold(INFO, namespace = "CensRCalc") # Reset logger to INFO level  lambda_c_to_plot <- seq(bounds[1], bounds[2], length.out = 100) cens_prop <- sapply(lambda_c_to_plot, estimator) plot(lambda_c_to_plot, cens_prop,   type = "l", xlab = expression(lambda[C]),   ylab = "Censoring Proportion" ) p_c <- 0.3 # Target censoring proportion  with_progress({   result <- find_cens_param(p_c, event_surv, cov_dens, cov_bounds,     time_accrual = tau_acc,     time_admin_cens = tau_adm,     cens_surv = cens_surv,     cens_dens = cens_dens,     target_bounds = bounds   )   print(result) }) #> $parameter #> [1] 2.499999 #>  #> $cens_prop #> [1] 0.3  lambda_c <- result$parameter set.seed(123)  n <- 10000 x <- runif(n, min = 1, max = 2) # Covariate t_true <- runif(n, min = 0, max = x) # Event times uniform (0, X) c_rnd <- runif(n, min = 0, max = lambda_c) # Random censoring times uniform r <- runif(n, min = 0, max = tau_acc) # Recruitment times uniform (0, tau_acc) c_adm <- tau_adm - r # title: Full Details and Usage
text: , use simplest distributions event censoring times, .e. uniform distributions: \[\begin{align*}     T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X} &\sim \text{U}(0, \lambda_{T^{*}}) \\     C_{\text{rnd}} &\sim \text{U}(0, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) \end{align*}\] \(\lambda_{T^{*}} = \beta_0 + \beta_1X\). Let \(\beta_0 = 0\), \(\beta_1 = 1\) \(X \sim \text{U}(1,2)\). Let \(\tau_{\text{acc}} = 1\), .e. patients accrued within one year time span. special case shown nothing aware setting \(\tau_{\text{acc}} = 0\). Furthermore, \(\tau_{\text{adm}} = 3\), .e. patients observed three years. means \(C_{\text{adm}} \sim U([2, 3])\). target value expected censoring proportion \(p_{C} = 0.3\). goal calculate parameter \(\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) random censoring distribution expected censoring proportion simulated dataset \(p_{C}\). calculating censoring probability specific subject, need survival functions event time, random censoring time administrative censoring time well density functions random administrative censoring time. survival functions given : \[\begin{align*}     S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(t) &= 1 - F_{T^{*}}(t) = 1 - \frac{t-0}{X-0} = \frac{X-t}{X} \\     S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(t) &= 1 - F_{C_{\text{rnd}}}(t) = 1 - \frac{t-0}{\lambda_{C_{rnd}}-0} = \frac{\lambda_{C_{rnd}}-t}{\lambda_{C_{rnd}}} \\     S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(t) &= 1 - F_{C_{\text{adm}}}(t) = 1 - \frac{t - (\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}})}{\tau_{\text{adm}} - (\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}})} = 1 - \frac{t - 2}{1} = 3 - t \end{align*}\] density functions given : \[\begin{align*}     f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(t) &= \frac{1}{\lambda_{C_{rnd}}-0} = \frac{1}{\lambda_{C_{rnd}}} \\     f_{C_{\text{adm}}}(t) &= \frac{1}{\tau_{\text{adm}} - (\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}})} = 1 \end{align*}\] probability calculated follows: \[\begin{align*}     P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) &= \!\begin{aligned}[t]                                                 &\int_{0}^{2} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} + \\                                                 &\int_{2}^{3} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} + \\                                                 &\int_{2}^{3} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{adm}})S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{adm}})f_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{adm}}) dc_{\text{adm}}                                             \end{aligned} \end{align*}\] Since support \(T^*\) \([0,X]\) \(X \[1,2]\), survival function \(S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(t) = 0\) \(t \geq 2\). Thus, second third integrals, integrate \([2,3]\), zero. first integral split two integrals: \[\begin{align*}     P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) &= \int_{0}^{2} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} \\     &= \int_{0}^{X} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} + \int_{X}^{2} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} \\ \end{align*}\] Using reason , second integral \([X,2]\), also zero. Thus, : \[\begin{align*}     P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) &= \int_{0}^{X} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} \\     &= \int_{0}^{X} \frac{X - c_{\text{rnd}}}{X} \cdot \frac{1}{\lambda_{C_{rnd}}} dc_{\text{rnd}} \\     &= \frac{1}{\lambda_{C_{rnd}} X} \int_{0}^{X} (X - c_{\text{rnd}}) dc_{\text{rnd}} \\     &= \frac{1}{\lambda_{C_{rnd}} X} \left[ X c_{\text{rnd}} - \frac{c_{\text{rnd}}^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{X} \\     &= \frac{1}{\lambda_{C_{rnd}} X} \left( X^2 - \frac{X^2}{2} \right) \\     &= \frac{X}{2 \lambda_{C_{rnd}}} \end{align*}\] Next calculate expected censoring proportion simulated dataset, independent covariates specific subject: \[\begin{align*}     P(\delta=0\mid\lambda_{C}) &= E_X\left[P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}, \lambda_{C})\right] \\     &= \int_{D_{\mathbf{X}}} P(\delta=0\mid\mathbf{X}=x, \lambda_{C_{rnd}})f_{X}(x)dx \\     &= \int_{1}^{2} \frac{X}{2 \lambda_{C_{rnd}}}f_{X}(x)dx \\     &= \int_{1}^{2} \frac{X}{2 \lambda_{C_{rnd}}} \cdot 1 dx \\     &= \frac{1}{2 \lambda_{C_{rnd}}} \int_{1}^{2}X dx \\     &= \frac{1}{2 \lambda_{C_{rnd}}} \left[\frac{X^2}{2} \right]_{1}^{2} \\     &= \frac{1}{4 \lambda_{C_{rnd}}} \left(4 - 1\right) \\     &= \frac{3}{4 \lambda_{C_{rnd}}} \end{align*}\] last step can calculate parameter \(\lambda_{C_{rnd}}\): \[\begin{align*}     &P(\delta=0\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) \overset{!}{=} 0.3 \\     &\leftrightarrow \frac{3}{4 \lambda_{C_{rnd}}} = 0.3 \\     &\leftrightarrow \frac{3}{4 \cdot 0.3} = \lambda_{C_{rnd}} \\     &\leftrightarrow \lambda_{C_{rnd}} = \frac{30}{12} = 2.5 \end{align*}\]

title: CensRCalc: Analytical Censoring Parameter Determination — CensRCalc
text: Let event time \(T^*\mid\mathbf{X}\sim F_{T^*\mid\mathbf{X}}\) survival function \(S_{T^*\mid\mathbf{X}}=1-F_{T^*\mid\mathbf{X}}\) random censoring time \(C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\sim F_{C_{\text{rnd}} \mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}\) survival function \(S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}=1-F_{C_{\text{rnd}} \mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}\), \(\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) random censoring parameter interest. Administrative censoring occurs time \(\tau_{\text{adm}}\). Accrual takes place \([0,\tau_{\text{acc}}]\) random accrual time \(R\sim U(0,\tau_{\text{acc}})\). equivalent random administrative censoring time accrual \(C_{\text{adm}}=\tau_{\text{adm}}-R\). Hence, \(C_{\text{adm}}\sim U(\tau_{\text{adm}}-\tau_{\text{acc}}, \tau_{\text{adm}})\). assumptions, probability censoring dependent \(\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) covariate vector \(\mathbf{X}\) \[ \begin{aligned} P(\delta=0\mid \mathbf{X},\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) = &\int_{0}^{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} + \\ &\int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(c_{\text{rnd}})S_{C_{\text{adm}}}(c_{\text{rnd}}) f_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(c_{\text{rnd}})dc_{\text{rnd}} + \\ &\int_{\tau_{\text{adm}} - \tau_{\text{acc}}}^{\tau_{\text{adm}}} S_{T^{*}\mid\mathbf{X}}(C_{\text{adm}}) S_{C_{\text{rnd}}\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}}(C_{\text{adm}}) f_{C_{\text{adm}}}(C_{\text{adm}})dc_{\text{adm}} \end{aligned} \] Next take expectation covariate distribution get expected censoring proportion: \[P(\delta=0\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}})=E_X\left[P(\delta=0\mid \mathbf{X},\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}})\right].\] implemented estimate_cens_prop(). obtain censoring parameter \(\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}\) achieves target censoring proportion \(p_C\), solve root finding problem \[P(\delta=0\mid\lambda_{C_{\text{rnd}}}) - p_C = 0\] Special cases include accrual time (\(\tau_{\text{acc}}=0\)) administrative censoring (\(\tau_{\text{adm}}=\infty\)). See package vignette vignette("full_details", package = "CensRCalc") details. Numerically, integrals evaluated using adaptive cubature (calculus::integral()), extended handle discrete mixed discrete/continuous covariates.
